Plan and Budget 2024
notes:
Craig Dyer, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer started the Plan and Budget 2024 presentation, outlining the 2024 budget committee review process, the preliminary 2024 operating budget, and the proposed use of tax stabilization reserve in the preliminary 2024 budget. He spoke to Regional tax levy funding for services that should be funded by Provincial revenues. The presentation focused on the strategic priority - Homes for All, with detailed discussion on senior housing and support, land readiness to attract investment and job creation, unlocking Region owned land to accelerate affordable housing, Waterloo Regional housing, and the Stage 2 Ion project.

In addressing a Committee inquiry, C. Dyer stated that the staff will report back with regards to the total Provincial impact, encompassing both reserve and levy funding. Additionally, the report will further explain the levy impact in the context of Provincial revenues for the year 2023-2024. 

In response to a question from the Committee, C. Dyer clarified that the majority of regional vehicles are not part of Grand River Transit (GRT). However, the reserves allocated for GRT are intended to support the funding of its capital program. Notably, the Tax Stabilization reserve is utilized to gradually accommodate the rising cost of fuel, and this phase-in is anticipated to extend into 2024.

Peter Sweeney, Commissioner, Community Services, continued the presentation, speaking to the Homes for All strategic priority. He highlighted services and current service levels, including housing and supports for seniors, making housing more affordable, homelessness, investment and economic vibrancy, regionally owned land, and improving stability for all. 

Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development & Legislative Services continued the presentation, further speaking to the Homes for All strategic initiative. He highlighted increasing the number and types of homes that are affordable and accessible, increase in housing and economic supports that address the needs of Indigenous, racialized, and other communities disproportionately affected by systemic inequity, and increase in land appropriately allocated to affordable housing, shovel-ready employment, and supportive infrastructure to meet our communities' future needs. 

P. Sweeney continued the presentation, outlining the proposed changes to senior services. Cheryl Braan, Director, Corporate Finance, explained the major budget drivers within the 2024 seniors' services budget. 

Addressing the Committee's query, Julie Wheeler, Director of Seniors' Services, discussed staffing models and clarified that the funding policy aims to facilitate the transition of staff from short shifts or part-time positions to optimal opportunities. Throughout the three-year investment period, the goal is to shift the staffing ratio from approximately 60% part-time to around 50% part-time

R. Regier continued the presentation, speaking the Homes for All through economic vibrancy and land readiness and the proposed changes. C. Braan spoke to the 2024 economic development budget. 

Responding to the Committee's inquiry, R. Regier offered additional insights regarding the proposed team expansion, emphasizing that it facilitates a smoother progression of development projects through the development process. He also addressed the consideration of community uses in the identification of regionally-owned lands for affordable housing.

Following direction from the Committee, C. Dyer stated that the staff will provide an update on the capital funding plan for industrial land readiness and development during the upcoming Strategic Planning and Budget Committee meeting on November 22, 2023.

In addressing a query from the Committee, R. Regier noted that the majority of the Economic Development team has been dedicated to fulfilling land readiness commitments. The team is currently operating at full capacity and is leveraging substantial resources from the Water Services, Transportation, and Finance teams to address housing needs. With upcoming major development initiatives in progress, staff are actively working to ensure that resources align with community expectations. Bruce Lauckner, Chief Administrative Officer, made further comments regarding staffing needs.

Continuing the presentation, R. Regier addressed the Region of Waterloo Airport (YKF), emphasizing its status as the fastest-growing airport in Canada and highlighting its strategic significance as an investment. He also discussed additional resources anticipated for the implementation of the Master Plan, set to commence in 2025.

In response to a question from the Committee, R. Regier highlighted that the airport master plan will prominently feature a significant component focused on sustainability. Addressing the industry-wide challenge of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and enhancing sustainability, the Region is committed to designing the airport infrastructure in a manner that optimizes for sustainability as part of the master plan.

P. Sweeney continued the presentation, outlining the key 2024 Strategic Initiatives directly supporting Homes for All. C. Braan spoke to the 2024 Housing Services budget.

In response to a question from the Committee, P. Sweeney addressed the waiting lists and timeframes for individuals waiting to secure housing units. He highlighted that one of the initiatives planned for 2024 is a thorough review of the waitlist to identify strategies for reducing wait times, ensuring a more realistic timeline. Additionally, staff will be developing a plan to establish a reasonable wait time. He further emphasized that staff will report back on the most frequently requested unit sizes at the next Strategic Planning and Budget meeting, November 22, 2023.

Committee members engaged in discussions on the operating budget related to internal housing, proposed staffing investments, and the progression through the housing system

Jerry Biersteker, Director, Facilities & Fleet Management, continued the presentation, outlining the Homes for All in Waterloo Region Housing (WRH) Facilities, including 420 Kingscourt Drive, 82 Wilson Avenue, and proposed changes. 

Members of the Committee engaged in discussion regarding accessibility, WRH maintenance work orders, and staffing. J. Biersteker responded to questions.

Jennifer Rose, Commissioner Engineering and Environmental Services, continued the presentation, speaking to Homes for All through design and construction, highlighting that projects in the capital plan will unlock Region-owned land for housing and economic development, the associated challenges, and proposed changes. 

C. Dyer concluded the presentation highlighting next steps.

items.title: COR-CFN-23-038, Options to Achieve Budget Guidelines (Staff Presentation)
notes:
C. Dyer provided a presentation regarding the options to achieve budget guidelines, speaking to the preliminary 2024 budget, annual efficiency review, options for budget reductions, capital and reserves, proposed staffing investments, and next steps.

In response to the question from the Committee, C. Dyer provided further clarification on the proposed staffing investments. He also mentioned that staff will provide information containing information on Full-Time Equivalents (FTEs) for 2022, projections for 2023, and the anticipated percentage increase for 2024.

Responding to a question from the Committee, R. Regier spoke to  the potential impact of Bill 23 on staffing costs and whether any reductions are reflected in the budget. He conveyed that the Region has anticipated ongoing costs up to the year 2024. He assured that adjustments will be made mid-year if deemed necessary. Additionally, he mentioned the commitment to provide further information on this matter for consideration in the 2025 budget

Responding to a question from the Committee with regards to whether the prior capital projects align with the region's new strategic priorities, C. Dyer explained that preliminary budget book encompasses a comprehensive list of capital projects for each division. Throughout the budget formulation process, each project has been meticulously assessed, and the majority of this evaluation has been concluded. J. Rose added that there is an ongoing refining project specifically focused on capital projects. The team is currently examining where each project fits within the broader strategic plan. She further noted that the presentation scheduled for November 29th will further address this.

items.title: Councillor D. McCabe
notes:
In her motion introduction, Councillor D. McCabe emphasized the importance of considering a future-focused request aimed at reducing waste and increasing the diversion rate, ultimately leading to cost reduction at Regional landfills. The motion aligns with the provincial organic framework, seeking to explore options through a staff report. It's clarified that this request does not commit the Region to any specific actions but rather aims to gather additional information for informed decision-making.

Committee members engaged in a discussion focused on construction material waste and the associated costs of operating landfill sites.

motions.text: WHEREAS three of the Region of Waterloo’s Strategic Plan pillars are Climate Aligned Growth, Equitable Services and Opportunities and Resilient and Future Ready Organization, and WHEREAS it is more efficient and cost-effective to reduce and divert waste from the waste management stream than to manage it within the waste management stream; and WHEREAS the provincial government has an Organics Framework with respect to the reduction and processing of organic material; and WHEREAS increased diversion of all materials from the landfill will lengthen the life of the landfill and defer and/or delay the cost of expanding the landfill; and WHEREAS increased diversion of organic material will reduce the emission of harmful methane gas; and WHEREAS developing community programs to divert textiles and healthy food from the waste stream will support equity deserving groups, reduce waste management costs and help to reduce GHG emissions; and WHEREAS with additional expertise the Region could work directly with residents, businesses and community partners to develop a waste diversion program for organics, textiles, electronics and other items that could continue to be used; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to report back November 29, 2023 on the potential to create a Waste Diversion strategy dedicated to working directly with the residents, businesses and community partners to increase waste diversion, the goal of which is to create upstream cost savings, reduce GHG emissions and delay the cost of expanding the landfill in alignment with the Region of Waterloo’s Strategic Plan pillars of Climate Aligned Growth, Equitable Services and Opportunities and Resilient and Future Ready Organization.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS three of the Region of Waterloo’s Strategic Plan pillars are Climate Aligned Growth, Equitable Services and Opportunities and Resilient and Future Ready Organization, and
 
WHEREAS it is more efficient and cost-effective to reduce and divert waste from the waste management stream than to manage it within the waste management stream; and 

WHEREAS the provincial government has an Organics Framework with respect to the reduction and processing of organic material; and
 
WHEREAS increased diversion of all materials from the landfill will lengthen the life of the landfill and defer and/or delay the cost of expanding the landfill; and 

WHEREAS increased diversion of organic material will reduce the emission of harmful methane gas; and
 
WHEREAS developing community programs to divert textiles and healthy food from the waste stream will support equity deserving groups, reduce waste management costs and help to reduce GHG emissions; and
 
WHEREAS with additional expertise the Region could work directly with residents, businesses and community partners to develop a waste diversion program for organics, textiles, electronics and other items that could continue to be used;
 
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to report back November 29, 2023 on the potential to create a Waste Diversion strategy dedicated to working directly with the residents, businesses and community partners to increase waste diversion, the goal of which is to create upstream cost savings, reduce GHG emissions and delay the cost of expanding the landfill in alignment with the Region of Waterloo’s Strategic Plan pillars of Climate Aligned Growth, Equitable Services and Opportunities and Resilient and Future Ready Organization.
